newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains against the dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains against the dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Monday despite a relatively low November consumer price index (CPI), dealers said.
The CPI rose 0.6 percent against a rise of 0.8 percent in October.

"The session opened with a slight rise of the dollar in response to the relatively low CPI. But, when the dollar reached 3.29 shekels investors started selling dollars and the U.S. currency fell to 3.28 shekels," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.

"For the last two weeks the dollar has been moving (in the local market) in a narrow range of 3.28 to 3.29 shekels. This trend is continuing and the market is looking for direction. In the long run I believe that the shekel will decline," the trader said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2810 shekels against 3.2830 shekels on Friday. The basket composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6608 shekels against 3.6702 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8816 shekels per 100 yen against 2.9020 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1090 shekels against 2.1258 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar continued to trade at 3.2800 shekels.
